record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.context_brief: conditional containment of CL in P
record.original_question: Can one prove that if L is a strict subset of P, then catalytic logspace CL is still contained in P?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Show that L ⊊ P implies CL ⊆ P.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let L denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using O(log n) work space, and let P denote the class of languages decidable in deterministic polynomial time. Catalytic logspace, denoted CL, is the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine equipped with: (i) a read-only input tape, (ii) a standard work tape of size O(log n), and (iii) an auxiliary "catalytic" tape of size 2^{O(log n)} = poly(n) that is initialized with an arbitrary string and must be restored to its exact initial contents by the end of the computation; the machine must accept/reject correctly for every initial content of the catalytic tape.

Prove the following conditional containment: if L ⊊ P (i.e., logspace is a strict subclass of polynomial time), then CL ⊆ P.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether CL ⊆ P (even unconditionally, or under the hypothesis L ⊊ P) remains a fundamental open problem in catalytic-space complexity. Recent works (2024–2025) have made progress on placing specific problems such as bipartite matching and linear matroid intersection into CL or CLP = CL ∩ P, but the general containment of CL inside P is still unresolved, with TC^1 being the strongest known upper bound on CL.

status_evidence.title: Linear Matroid Intersection is in Catalytic Logspace
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works place specific P-problems in CL; the general inclusion CL ⊆ P remains open.
status_evidence.claim: CL ⊆ P is not established; ongoing work focuses on individual problems in CL.

status_evidence.title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
status_evidence.snippet: First well-studied subclass of P known to compute MATCH; CL ⊆ P remains open and TC^1 is the strongest known containment.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Logspace: Complexity & Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Understanding CL remains a major open problem; TC^1 is the most powerful containment to date.
status_evidence.claim: CL ⊆ P is an open problem.
